To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incumbent firm is better off if it sponsors intra-technology competition.
the incumbent firm prefers intra-technology competition when the rival technology has a lower cost advantage, and prefers inter-technology competition when it has a higher cost advantage.
the incumbent firm prefers to sponsor intra-competition over inter-competition, unless the rival technology is sufficiently cheap to produce, or if the incumbent is sufficiently cheap to imitate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the incumbent firm can profit from the entry of a new technology or whether its superior technology is threatened by the entry of a competing technology.
the strategic choice of the incumbent firm in a market characterized by incompatible technologies and network externalities.
the following issues: (i) How should a firm choose between intra- and inter-technology competition when it faces the strategic decision to license its technology to a rival?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incumbent firm is better off by sponsoring intra-technology rather than inter-technology competition if the incumbent firm has a cost advantage over its rival.
, depending on the relative cost advantages, the incumbent firm may either prefer to sponsor intra-competition or to insist on an inter-technology competition.
the incumbent firm should share its technology with a rival when the latterAEs cost advantage is sufficiently small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incumbent firm prefers inter-technology competition when it has a cost disadvantage and prefers intra-technology competition when the cost advantage is sufficiently large.
the incumbent firm should not sponsor intra-technology competitions.
, in a network market, the incumbent firm has an advantage over the rival firm if the incumbent firm has a lower cost of production and the network size of the incumbent firm is sufficiently high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incumbent firm will prefer intra-technology competition when its cost advantage is large enough, and it will prefer inter-technology competition otherwise.
the incumbent firm may choose to sponsor intra-competition if it is sufficiently cost advantaged, and it may choose inter-competition if the cost disadvantage of its rival is sufficiently large.
the incumbent firm is better off sponsoring intra-technology than inter-technology competition, even though the former may result in a higher market share for the rival.
